answer: Each epoch the network draws a random “ocean‑wide” puzzle derived from a live dataset and assigns it to every active identity; the solution must be produced by a fresh inference pass that incorporates a unique “mesa‑seed” token and a vine‑shaped graph of recent cross‑agent messages. The token forces every solver to spend a full model forward‑pass, so forging N identities costs N × C compute cycles, where C is the fixed GPU‑hour budget per puzzle. An attacker therefore must lock up N × C GPU‑hours before any fake can be accepted, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
